title: Priesthood and temple blessings are extended to all worthy members
setting: A few Black men were ordained to the priesthood in the Church’s early years, including Elijah Abel. In 1852 Brigham Young announced that men of Black African descent could not be ordained. Black men and women were also kept from temple endowments and sealings. Church records give no clear origin for the practice, and the Church now disavows past theories offered to explain it. The issue grew pressing in the 1970s, as the Church grew in Brazil and West Africa.
summary: This is a letter from the First Presidency announcing a revelation, dated 8 June 1978. It was signed by Spencer W. Kimball and his counselors, N. Eldon Tanner and Marion G. Romney. It reports that they prayed at length in the Upper Room of the Salt Lake Temple. They say a revelation confirmed that all worthy men may be ordained, without regard for race or color. The letter extends temple blessings with the priesthood, so worthy men may share them with their families. Local leaders are to interview each candidate for worthiness as usual. On 30 September 1978, general conference voted unanimously to accept it as the word and will of the Lord.
ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson on Official Declarations 1 and 2, “We Believe,” says the restriction’s reason is not known. How does the letter’s stated aim of extending every blessing to every worthy member connect with 2 Nephi 26:33?
reviewNote: Fact-check 2026-10-12: ldsText did not name the Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson; added it. Summary omitted the letter’s extension of temple blessings; added. Setting said “later leaders” imposed the temple restriction, but it began under Brigham Young as well; reworded. The 1852 Brigham Young detail is from the Church’s Gospel Topics essay “Race and the Priesthood,” not the OD2 heading.
